title: Adobe token response members that are not credential values
summary: Members of an Adobe token response or request that are not credential values: a client id, the token type, the expiry in seconds and the scope list, and an access or refresh token member that holds a placeholder, an environment reference, a template reference or a masked display.
rationale: The client id, token_type, expires_in and scope are public configuration or lifetime facts, not the token. A placeholder or reference stands in for a value kept elsewhere, and a masked display has no recoverable value. Protecting any of these would redact text a reader needs and would extend the member claim beyond what it states.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Not flagged under project policy: the values here are identifiers, placeholders, references, masked text or non-secret outputs, not credential values. That a placeholder or reference is not a value is a project decision, not a Adobe statement.

sources.supports: Sample response shows access_token, token_type bearer and expires_in; no refresh token is used for OAuth Server-to-Server credentials.
Response object: refresh_token, generated refresh token, by default expires in 14 days; only present if offline_access was requested and consented.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
